Lessons.Title: Write Division Expressions
ExplanationParagraphs: Division with equal groups has two questions: how many groups are needed, or how many are in each group? Write total ÷ KNOWN group quantity. The divisor may be a group count or group size; the quotient represents the unknown.
Warm-up (10 min), What's the Same?: 225−100,227−102,230−105 and220−95 all equal125. A number-line explanation can move both endpoints equally without changing their difference.

Activity1 (15 min), Card Sort: All about Bugs: the 2021 public student cards comprise six contexts A–F. A:10 digging legs from5 mole crickets→10÷5=2 per cricket; B:8 antennae at2 per beetle→8÷2=4 beetles; C:14 antennae at2 per bee→14÷2=7 bees; D:12 wings at4 per dragonfly→12÷4=3 dragonflies; E:30 legs from5 ants→30÷5=6 per ant; F:50 spots from5 butterflies→50÷5=10 per butterfly.

Classify A,E,F as 'how many IN each group?' because the number of animals is given. Classify B,C,D as 'how many GROUPS?' because the number of objects per animal is given. Ask each pupil to justify the number named by divisor and the unit named by quotient. Partner sorting, physical cards and MLR8 discussion are teacher-evaluated, not scalar graded.

Activity2 (20 min), Solve a Buggy Problem: students prepare a group visual display with diagrams, wording and a solution for an assigned previous card; teacher facilitates a gallery walk (MLR7 Compare and Connect). An integer answer alone is insufficient to certify that display.

Lesson synthesis: two columns compare unknown number of groups and unknown size within each group. Student Section Summary: Han has12 pencils, packs2 per box→6 boxes (6×2 drawing). Elena has12 pencils and2 boxes→6 per box (2×6 drawing). Both stories use12÷2 but the drawings and answer units differ.

The original Ant Legs publisher Cool-down requires teacher login and was not reproduced. Source insect photo and blackline card master were not pixel-verified; Edulytics dots and exercises are independent authoring. Stage D/CI/academic signoff has not occurred.

KeyConcepts.Title: Number of groups unknown
KeyConcepts.Definition: Total and fixed number in each group are known.

KeyConcepts.Title: Size of each group unknown
KeyConcepts.Definition: Total and count of equal groups are known.
KeyConcepts.Example: 10 cricket legs from5 crickets→2 special legs each

KeyConcepts.Title: Same expression, different meaning
KeyConcepts.Definition: The divisor is the known quantity whose unit comes from the context.
KeyConcepts.Rule: 12÷2 may mean 12 pencils into2 boxes OR2 pencils in each box.
KeyConcepts.Example: Elena has2 boxes of6; Han has6 boxes of2.

KeyConcepts.Title: Constant difference
KeyConcepts.Definition: Add the same value to both terms of subtraction.

WorkedExamples.Title: Sort six insect cards
WorkedExamples.Question: For each bug card, write the division expression and classify the unknown.
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify total and whether animals count or items per animal are given.
Steps: A10÷5=2 legs per cricket (size); B8÷2=4 beetles (count).
E30÷5=6 legs per ant (size); F50÷5=10 spots per butterfly (size).
Group-count B,C,D; group-size A,E,F; teacher separately checks card reasoning.
WorkedExamples.Answer: A2 B4 C7 D3 E6 F10; A/E/F group size and B/C/D group count.
WorkedExamples.Check: Re-multiply group count by objects in each for all six.

WorkedExamples.Title: One expression, two drawings
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare Han’s12 pencils in boxes at2 each with Elena’s12 pencils in2 equal boxes.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use labels for the divisor and an independently drawn set of groups.
Steps: Elena:12÷2=6 per box; draw2 groups of6.
Explain why the same numerical answer six has different units and group diagrams.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Han6 boxes, Elena6 pencils per box.

WorkedExamples.Title: Invariant difference
WorkedExamples.Question: Why do 225−100 and230−105 both equal125?
Steps: 230−105 adds5 to BOTH minuend and subtrahend.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: All six bug cards ask the number of bugs.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A/E/F ask legs or spots per specified number of bugs.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Group by unknown, not merely by insect context.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use the insect count as divisor even when unknown.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: For card B there are8 antennae at2 per beetle; the beetle count4 is the QUOTIENT.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claim same expression implies same grouping drawing.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Han’s6 boxes of2 differ from Elena’s2 boxes of6.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Represent known group count and objects per group separately.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Turn a teacher poster/gallery assessment into numeric-only success.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The task requires collaborative visual reasoning and discussion.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Mark open representation and explanation for teacher review.

SummaryPoints: Bug expressions A10÷5, B8÷2, C14÷2, D12÷4, E30÷5, F50÷5.
B,C,D ask group count; A,E,F ask group size.
Han12÷2→6 groups of2; Elena12÷2→2 groups of6.
